newsitem.title: EGYPT: New Egypt-Kuwait co. in $30 mln share offer. [CORRECTED 16:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: New Egypt-Kuwait co. in $30 mln share offer. [CORRECTED 16:45 GMT]

text.p: An Egyptian-Kuwaiti investment company under establishment said on Friday it was offering for sale to the public three million shares worth $30 million.

The sale would cover a quarter of the company's total number of shares and is to begin in at least 15 days from Friday, said the Egyptian-Kuwaiti Holding Company in an official announcement in al-Ahram newspaper.
The company invited applications from the public to buy a minimum of 500 shares of the three million it was offering at a fixed price of $10 per share.
The offer will remain open for 60 days but the company has the right to close it at least 10 days into the offer if it is oversubscribed.
It said the offer is open to Egyptians and non-Egyptians, particularly nationals of the Gulf Cooperation Council, which comprised Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, United Arab Emirates, Oman and Bahrain.

The announcement described the company as an Egyptian stock venture under establishment with authorised capital of $500 million (corrects from $5 billion) and issued and paid up capital of $120 million (corrects from $12 billion).
The company said its work would cover mainly the sale and promotion of securities.
The remaining 75 percent of the company's shares are owned by Egyptian and Kuwaiti companies and business people.
They include Misr Foam/Egyptian Sponge, Kuwait's Mohammed Abdel-Mohsen al-Khorafi and Sons Company and member of the Kuwaiti royal family Soad Mohammed al-Sabah.
Egypt and Kuwait last year signed an agreement on working towards the introduction of mutual trade in Egyptian and Kuwaiti shares.
Kuwaiti officials said the mutual trade envisaged by the pact with Egypt would be the most far-reaching between any two Arab stock exchanges.
Brokers from the Lebanese, Egyptian and Kuwait stock exchanges signed agreements to start cross-trading equities.
